stations.title: Seed Library Map Room
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for a calm independent desk, co-op table, or tutoring rotation using a seed-map story plan.
stations.kidDirection: Choose a seed drawer, map a tiny route, and write the first note for the map room helper.
stations.subNote: Use this station when students can work quietly from a printed page; invented plant names are enough.

pageSections.heading: Seed Drawer
lines: The seed drawer label says ____________________________.
The tiny seed packet holds ____________________________.
The map room shelf is marked with ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Map Route
lines: The first map turn goes past ____________________________.
The second map clue is hidden near ____________________________.
The final map mark points toward ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Helper Note
lines: First, the helper plants the idea of ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: One map-room detail I want to keep is ____________________________.

stations.title: Index Card Theater Club
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for older elementary writers to plan a tiny scene with index-card roles and a short dialogue beat.
stations.kidDirection: Pick a theater card, choose a scene job, and write a short exchange that moves the story forward.
stations.subNote: Partners may read ideas quietly, but each writer should complete a separate page.

pageSections.heading: Scene Card
lines: The theater card names a place called ____________________________.
The card asks one character to carry ____________________________.
The scene job for this card is ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Dialogue Beat
lines: The second speaker answers ____________________________.
The dialogue changes the plan by ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Stage Direction
lines: At the start, the character stands near ____________________________.
In the middle, the character notices ____________________________.
At the end, the scene points toward ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: The line that best moves my scene is ____________________________.

stations.title: Margin Note Market
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for revision practice, early finishers, or a quiet table where students trade stronger details.
stations.kidDirection: Visit the margin note stalls, trade a weak detail for a stronger one, and write the revised sentence.
stations.subNote: Use this as a no-pressure revision page; one improved sentence is a complete station outcome.

pageSections.heading: Market Stall
lines: The first margin stall offers ____________________________.
The second margin stall trades for ____________________________.
The note seller recommends ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Detail Trade
lines: A plain detail on my page is ____________________________.
A stronger detail I can trade in is ____________________________.
The sentence changes because ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Revised Line
lines: Before revision, the sentence was about ____________________________.
After revision, the sentence includes ____________________________.
The improved sentence is ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: One revision choice that helped my writing is ____________________________.

stations.title: Clue Label Tower Museum
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for a museum-label style activity that builds precise nouns, clues, and a short exhibit note.
stations.kidDirection: Create three exhibit labels, choose the clearest clue, and write the tower museum note.
stations.subNote: This station rewards precise words; students can finish with labels instead of a long draft.

pageSections.heading: Exhibit Labels
lines: The first exhibit is labeled ____________________________.
The second exhibit is labeled ____________________________.
The third exhibit is labeled ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Clue Choice
lines: The clearest clue is hidden beside ____________________________.
The clue matters because ____________________________.
The tower guide notices ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Museum Note
lines: Next, the guide adds a label for ____________________________.
The exhibit note explains ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: The most precise exhibit word I chose is ____________________________.

stations.title: Revision River Ferry
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for a calm revision ferry route where students move one draft idea from rough to clearer.
stations.kidDirection: Load one sentence onto the ferry, cross the revision river, and unload a clearer version.
stations.subNote: A student may revise a sentence from this page or invent a new rough sentence to polish.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Load
lines: The rough sentence starts with ____________________________.
The ferry carries one detail about ____________________________.
The sentence needs clearer words for ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: River Crossing
lines: At the second dock, I remove ____________________________.
At the third dock, I choose the stronger word ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Clearer Unload
lines: The revised sentence now shows ____________________________.
The detail that changed most is ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: One word I improved on the ferry is ____________________________.

stations.title: Compass Craft Academy
stations.stationUse: Substitute-day printable writing station for a self-directed craft-academy plan using directions, materials, and a short procedure-style scene.
stations.kidDirection: Choose a compass craft, list the materials, and write the first three steps of the academy plan.
stations.subNote: Small groups may brainstorm materials together, then each writer completes a separate plan.

pageSections.heading: Craft Choice
lines: The academy craft is called ____________________________.
The compass points toward ____________________________.
The craft helps the story character by ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Material List
lines: The first invented material is ____________________________.
The second invented material is ____________________________.
The safest classroom substitute for drawing it is ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Academy Plan
lines: Step one of the craft plan is ____________________________.
Step two of the craft plan is ____________________________.
Step three of the craft plan is ____________________________.

stations.exitTicketLine: The clearest academy step I wrote is ____________________________.
